tier1.head: Ontology identifiers here are model-emitted and largely unverified.
tier1.body: Roughly 42% of Tier 1 identifiers do not denote the entity on their own row (`id_denotes_entity_rate` = 0.578, a lower bound). The model wrote them; nothing looked them up. Every one is tagged `ontology_id_verification == 'unverified_model_emitted'`. **Do not treat a non-null identifier here as an authority-grounded mapping.** Tiers 3 and 4 derive identifiers from names by resolver lookup and score 0.986 / 0.998.

tier1.head: Paper count is 3,129 here, not the 3,121 of the Tier 1 v1 release.
tier1.body: The v1 release counted `canonical_pmid.nunique()`, which merged 8 duplicate-title records. That column does not exist in the harmonized corpus. Both numbers are correct under their own basis; this package uses `pmid.nunique()` throughout.

tier1.head: `canonical_entity` is empty in this package.
tier1.body: Cross-tier canonicalization was applied to Tiers 3 and 4 only. The lookup covering all five packages ships as `data/entity_vocabulary_crosstier.parquet` — join on `entity` to canonicalize Tier 1 yourself. It mutates no rows by design.

tier2a.head: This is one half of Tier 2. Part B is a separate package.
tier2a.body: Tier 2 was extracted in two waves. This package is the first wave: {n_chunks} chunks, {findings} findings, {papers} papers. The two waves share **zero papers** and their chunk ids interleave, so neither is a clean 'earlier literature' or 'later literature' split — the division is operational, not topical. Both parts cover the same nine themes. Pool them freely: they came from one pipeline with one prompt, and every column has identical semantics across the two.

tier2a.head: `ontology_id_source == 'unresolved_nulled'` means the identifier was KEPT.
tier2a.body: In Tiers 3 and 4 the same value means the identifier was NULLED. The obvious filter `df[df.ontology_id_source != 'unresolved_nulled']` silently drops Tier 2 rows that DO carry identifiers. Use `ontology_id_verification` instead. See COMPARABILITY.md, Trap 3.

tier2a.head: Ontology identifiers here are model-emitted.
tier2a.body: `id_denotes_entity_rate` for Tier 2 is 0.708 — roughly 29% of identifiers do not denote the entity on their row (a lower bound). **That figure was measured on Tier 2 as a whole, from a 270-row adjudicated sample spanning both waves, and is inherited by this package; no per-wave rate exists.** Tier 2 has the HIGHEST identifier coverage and the SECOND-WORST identifier correctness in the corpus. See COMPARABILITY.md, Trap 1.

tier3.head: Identifiers here are authority-derived and score 0.986.
tier3.body: The extraction model emitted names only; a resolver looked every identifier up afterwards. This is the property Tiers 1 and 2 lack. All nine invariants pass.

tier3.head: 40 rows are flagged `query_contamination`.
tier3.body: Six papers were pulled in by the ambiguous abbreviation 'ASD' — adult spinal deformity and atrial septal defect, not autism. Filter with `df[~df.query_contamination.fillna(False)]`. The 28 wrong-ASD PMIDs are listed in `scope/tier3_offtopic_pmids.csv`. Note that `query_contamination` means something DIFFERENT in Tier 4 — see COMPARABILITY.md.

tier3.head: Shipped-source verifiability is the lowest in the corpus at 12.22%.
tier3.body: Tier 3 had the highest full-text retrieval success (69% of papers), and full text was discarded after extraction — so its very success is why so few of its quotes have a shipped source. The v1.1 retrofit re-fetched every paper and re-checked every quote (99.96% now have a checkable source; see the Annotations section and `annotations/quote_retrofit_tier3.parquet`), against Europe PMC's current text rather than a retained archive.

tier4.head: Every quote in this package is verifiable — the only package where that is true.
tier4.body: Body text was retained in gzipped chunk archives, so all 15,646 rows can be re-checked against their own source. {corpus_wide} Traceability measured 99.09% with 0% wrong-paper false positives.

tier4.head: Identifiers are authority-derived and score 0.998 — the highest in the corpus.
tier4.body: Note that Tier 4 also has the LOWEST identifier coverage (10.3% of rows). Coverage and correctness rank the packages in opposite orders; see COMPARABILITY.md, Trap 1.

tier4.head: 1,960 rows are flagged `screen_verdict_uncertain`, and coverage has two true values.
tier4.body: Tier 4 papers passed an LLM+rule screen because its themes (migraine, Sjögren's, PANS/PANDAS, hypermobility spectrum) sit at the corpus boundary. Coverage is 85.97% of screened papers and 74.57% of the pre-screening universe. Both are true; state which you mean. Excluded PMIDs with reasons are in `scope/`.

tier2b.head: This is one half of Tier 2. Part A is a separate package.
tier2b.body: Tier 2 was extracted in two waves. This package is the second wave: {n_chunks} chunks, {findings} findings, {papers} papers. The two waves share **zero papers** and their chunk ids interleave, so neither is a clean 'earlier literature' or 'later literature' split — the division is operational, not topical. Both parts cover the same nine themes. Pool them freely: they came from one pipeline with one prompt, and every column has identical semantics across the two.

tier2b.head: `ontology_id_source == 'unresolved_nulled'` means the identifier was KEPT.
tier2b.body: In Tiers 3 and 4 the same value means the identifier was NULLED. The obvious filter `df[df.ontology_id_source != 'unresolved_nulled']` silently drops Tier 2 rows that DO carry identifiers. Use `ontology_id_verification` instead. See COMPARABILITY.md, Trap 3.

tier2b.head: Ontology identifiers here are model-emitted.
tier2b.body: `id_denotes_entity_rate` for Tier 2 is 0.708 — roughly 29% of identifiers do not denote the entity on their row (a lower bound). **That figure was measured on Tier 2 as a whole, from a 270-row adjudicated sample spanning both waves, and is inherited by this package; no per-wave rate exists.** Tier 2 has the HIGHEST identifier coverage and the SECOND-WORST identifier correctness in the corpus. See COMPARABILITY.md, Trap 1.

readme_warning_fidelity.head: Scientific fidelity is UNMEASURED.
readme_warning_fidelity.body: Everything verified in `qa/` is well-formedness: quotes trace to source, identifiers carry authority provenance, invariants hold. **Nobody has checked that the extracted science is correctly interpreted.** That needs a human reader — an LLM adjudicator shares the extractor's blind spots. Treat every row as a pointer to a paper you should read, not as a fact.

id_provenance.tier1: 4,373 rows carry a resolved ontology id and 2,681 carry an HGNC id, with no source tag. Tier 1 predates the provenance-tag convention entirely — `ontology_id_source` is null for every Tier 1 row. The identifiers are model-emitted and existence-checked only; the harmonized columns `ontology_id_verification` and `ontology_id_match_mode` record that fact explicitly. This is a KNOWN, DOCUMENTED property of Tier 1, not a defect introduced by packaging.
id_provenance.tier2a: 1,243 rows carry a resolved ontology id and 5,714 an HGNC id whose source tag is absent or reads `unresolved_nulled` — which in Tier 2 means the identifier was KEPT (see COMPARABILITY.md, Trap 3). Tier 2's tag vocabulary (`authority_lookup_B/C/D`) records neither ontology nor match mode. KNOWN and DOCUMENTED; use the harmonized verification columns instead.
id_provenance.tier2b: 999 rows carry a resolved ontology id and 5,232 an HGNC id whose source tag is absent or reads `unresolved_nulled` — which in Tier 2 means the identifier was KEPT (see COMPARABILITY.md, Trap 3). KNOWN and DOCUMENTED; use the harmonized verification columns instead.

no_model_emitted_ids.tier2a: 11 rows from a single paper (PMID 41449404) carry GO identifiers inside the free-text `pathway_or_mechanism` field, e.g. 'Presynaptic modulation of chemical synaptic transmission (GO:0099171)'. The model wrote them into a prose field. They are NOT used as identifiers anywhere — `pathway_id` was dropped from the schema — so nothing downstream consumes them. Left verbatim rather than stripped: the rule is to flag, never silently repair. Filter with a regex on `pathway_or_mechanism` if a clean prose field matters to you.
no_model_emitted_ids.tier2b: 1 row from PMID 40338225 carries GO identifiers inside the free-text `pathway_or_mechanism` field ('Pathogen detection pathway (GO:0016045, GO:0016032, GO:0098543)'). Not consumed as an identifier anywhere. Left verbatim rather than stripped — flag, never silently repair.

invariant_failure_footer: The suite was written during Tier 3 and encodes conventions Tiers 1 and 2 predate. These are
**pre-existing, characterized properties of the earlier extraction passes**, not damage from
packaging. They are shipped as failures rather than suppressed because the project rule is to
flag and never silently repair — a suite tuned until it passes is not a suite. The harmonized
`ontology_id_verification` / `ontology_id_match_mode` columns exist precisely so that a query
can respect this without reading the invariant output.
enum_drift_notes: `systematic-review/meta-analysis` and `systematic review` are the model splitting a distinction the enum collapses into `meta-analysis`. Arguably the enum is the deficient one — a systematic review without a pooled estimate is not a meta-analysis.
`case-report/case-series` is the model refusing to choose between two adjacent enum values that the source genuinely straddles.
`other patient group` marks findings about a different disease used as a mechanistic analogy. The enum has no slot for that, so this is an enum deficiency, formally unadjudicated.

`IBD_gut` is probably a typo for `IBS_gut` — but inflammatory bowel disease and irritable bowel syndrome are different diseases, so auto-correcting it would be a guess that changes what a row claims. Left as-is, flagged, unadjudicated.
`orthostatic_hypotension` is a real and clinically distinct condition that the enum omits; it is adjacent to but not the same as POTS.
readme_schema_evolution_caveat: ### A note on `certainty_derived` and other Tier-3-onward columns
Several columns were introduced partway through the project and are **entirely empty** in the
`hpo_ids_verified`, `phenotype_terms`. In those packages a null means **the property was never
captured**, not that it was measured and found absent.
The `cap_*` flags exist so a query can tell the difference without consulting documentation:
df.cap_entity_kind.iloc[0]   # False -> this tier does not carry entity_kind at all
`docs/DATA_DICTIONARY.md` lists every empty column in this package.
annotations_intro: The tables below were produced AFTER the tier data was frozen and ship as separate, ADDITIVE
files. No row of `data/` was modified. Join them on the stated key; every rate they carry states
its numerator, denominator and basis. They are covered by `MANIFEST.json` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256`.

quote_retrofit.parquet.desc: Per-row quote traceability against source text re-fetched from Europe PMC on 2026-09-16, with source depth, fetch status and the wrong-paper control. Null `retrofit_traceable` means no source exists today.

condition_annotations.parquet.desc: Per-paper verdict on the `condition == 'MCAS'` bucket under population-studied semantics (`in_bucket` / `bucket_violation` / `NEEDS_HUMAN`), classifier-derived, none human-confirmed.

retrofit_fetch_log.parquet.desc: One row per Tier 1–3 paper attempted in the retrofit: abstract/full-text availability, PMCID, HTTP outcome, fetch date.

retrofit_summary.json.desc: Machine-readable retrofit numbers for all four Tier 1–3 packages, every rate with numerator, denominator and basis.

RETROFIT_REPORT.md.desc: The retrofit report: deviations, per-stratum rates with controls, itemised permanent losses, untraceable examples.

CONDITION_ANNOTATIONS_README.md.desc: Schema and coverage of condition_annotations, and how to join it.

CONDITION_BUCKET_DEFINITIONS.md.desc: v1 written definitions of the `condition` buckets (MCAS decided; others provisional) and the MCAS census that prompted them.

COMPARATOR_GATE.json.desc: Regression gate run before the retrofit: the shipped comparator reproduces Tier 4's 99.09% and is entity-code symmetric (42/42).

column_descriptions.entity: Marker, gene, protein, metabolite or measure the finding is about. Free text as the model wrote it. Null on 40%+ of rows by design — symptom, phenotype and quality-of-life findings name no entity.
column_descriptions.entity_ontology_id: Model-emitted ontology identifier. **Tiers 1-2 only.** Never authority-verified. Do not use as a mapping; use `entity_ontology_id_resolved` with `ontology_id_verification`.
column_descriptions.gene_marker: Gene symbol as written in the source.
column_descriptions.direction: Direction of the effect (increased / decreased / unchanged / etc.).
column_descriptions.direction_reference: What the direction is relative to (controls, baseline, another group).
column_descriptions.finding_text: The extracted finding, one sentence, as the model rendered it.
column_descriptions.pathway_or_mechanism: Free-text mechanism. Prose, not an ontology term — only 14 of 147 Tier-2 mechanism strings were real ontology terms, which is why `pathway_id` was dropped.
column_descriptions.pathway_id: **Tiers 1-2 only, 0.1% filled.** Deprecated; no single GO/Reactome term denotes most mechanism prose.
column_descriptions.quantitative_detail: Numeric detail as stated in the source.
column_descriptions.effect_size: Effect size as stated. Not harmonized across studies.
column_descriptions.causal_or_correlational: Whether the source claims causation or correlation.
column_descriptions.evidence_tier: Study design. Pinned enum; drift is flagged, never coerced — see the README.
column_descriptions.condition: What the finding is ABOUT. Distinct from `source_literature` (which literature it came from).
column_descriptions.pots_subtype: POTS subtype where the source specifies one.
column_descriptions.is_covid_associated: Whether the finding concerns a COVID-associated population. Semantics differ subtly by tier — see comparability report.
column_descriptions.finding_type: Kind of finding (biomarker, mechanism, treatment response, prevalence, …).
column_descriptions.treatment_class: Treatment class where the finding concerns one.
column_descriptions.phenotype_hpo: **Model-emitted HPO identifier, Tiers 1-2. ~34% were fabricated.** Do not use. Use `hpo_ids_verified`.
column_descriptions.adverse_event_note: Adverse event mentioned alongside the finding.
column_descriptions.certainty: The extractor's own certainty judgment. Never overwritten.
column_descriptions.dataset_accession: Dataset accession where stated. 0.7% filled — papers rarely state one.
column_descriptions.provenance_quote: **The verbatim source span the finding was drawn from.** The verification handle for the whole dataset. Present on every row. See LICENSE for terms — this column is not CC BY.
column_descriptions.provenance_section: Which section of the paper the quote came from.
column_descriptions.null_or_failed_result: Set where the finding is a null or failed result — deliberately retained, since these are systematically under-published.
column_descriptions.contradicts_finding_ref: Reference to a finding this one contradicts.
column_descriptions.is_duplicate_or_preprint_note: Note where the source may be a duplicate or preprint of another record.
column_descriptions.contradicts_or_extends: Whether the finding contradicts or extends prior work.
column_descriptions.pmid: PubMed ID. **The paper key. Count papers with `pmid.nunique()`.**
column_descriptions.title: Paper title.
column_descriptions.source_stream: Which query stream retrieved the paper.
column_descriptions.theme: Extraction theme. Package-specific vocabulary by construction — never compare across packages.
column_descriptions.fulltext_status: `retrieved-fulltext` / `abstract-only` / `blocked`. **Drives yield ~3x and determines verifiability.** Always stratify on this.
column_descriptions.chunk_id: Extraction chunk. Maps to the tier via `chunk_order.parquet`.
column_descriptions.gene_resolved: Whether the gene symbol resolved against an authority.
column_descriptions.entity_ontology_id_resolved: Resolved ontology identifier. **Meaning differs by tier: authority-derived in Tiers 3-4, model-emitted in Tiers 1-2.** Always read alongside `ontology_id_verification`.
column_descriptions.entity_ontology_label: The authority's own label for the identifier. Comparing this to `entity` is how identifier correctness was measured offline.
column_descriptions.source_fidelity: Retained for forward compatibility. **Single value on many packages — zero information. Not a quality filter that passed.**
column_descriptions.source_route: How the source text was obtained.
column_descriptions.tier_source: Which extraction pass produced the row (`t1`/`t2`/`t3`/`t4`). Constant within a package.
column_descriptions.cap_entity_kind: **Capability flag** (computed): does this row's tier support `entity_kind`? Null means NOT PRESENT, not unknown.
column_descriptions.cap_hpo_verified: **Capability flag**: does this tier carry authority-verified HPO identifiers?
column_descriptions.cap_number_in_quote: **Capability flag**: does this tier carry the `number_in_quote` check?
column_descriptions.cap_quote_source_retained: **Capability flag**: is the quote's own source text still retained? True only in Tier 4.
column_descriptions.ontology_id_verification: **Added by harmonization. Consistent semantics across all five packages — filter on THIS.** `authority_verified` (Tiers 3-4) / `unverified_model_emitted` (Tiers 1-2) / `no_id`.
column_descriptions.ontology_id_match_mode: **Added by harmonization.** How the identifier was matched (exact label, synonym, …).
column_descriptions.hpo_verification: **Added by harmonization.** HPO verification status, consistent across packages.
column_descriptions.hpo_id_count_unified: Number of verified HPO identifiers on the row, unified across packages.
column_descriptions.ontology_id_prefix: Ontology namespace of the identifier (HGNC, CHEBI, HP, …).
column_descriptions.ontology_id_repaired: Whether the syntactic repair pass touched this identifier. **Syntactic only — case and namespace. Re-derived nothing from names.**
column_descriptions.ontology_id_source: **TRAP: inverted semantics across tiers.** `unresolved_nulled` means identifier KEPT in Tier 2 and identifier NULLED in Tiers 3-4. Provenance only — never a filter. See COMPARABILITY.md.
column_descriptions.entity_kind: Entity type (gene, protein, chemical/metabolite, …). **Tiers 3-4 only** — null means NOT PRESENT in Tiers 1-2.
column_descriptions.phenotype_terms: Atomic clinical terms split out of the raw symptom string.
column_descriptions.certainty_derived: Hedge-detection over both `finding_text` and `provenance_quote`: both hedged -> hedged, neither -> confirmed, disagreement -> mixed. Never overwrites `certainty`.
column_descriptions.number_in_quote: Is the value in `quantitative_detail`/`effect_size` actually present in the quote? ~9.9% of Tier-2 rows fail. **A genuine open question, not a bug to auto-fix.**
column_descriptions.fetch_note: HTTP status or exception from the fetch, so `blocked` is diagnosable rather than terminal.
column_descriptions.hpo_ids_verified: **Authority-verified HPO identifiers, semicolon-delimited.** Multi-value because 43.2% of mappable symptom strings resolve to more than one HPO term.
column_descriptions.hpo_labels_verified: Labels for the verified HPO identifiers.
column_descriptions.hpo_id_count: Count of semicolon-delimited HPO identifiers. Invariant-checked against the string.
column_descriptions._source_version_id: Build provenance: which per-tier artifact the row came from.
column_descriptions.canonical_entity: Canonical entity name. **Tiers 3-4 only in-row.** Join `entity_vocabulary_crosstier.parquet` to canonicalize Tiers 1-2.
column_descriptions.source_literature: Which condition literature the paper was drawn FROM. Distinct from `condition` (what the finding is about).
column_descriptions.about_condition: Condition the finding is about, harmonized.
column_descriptions.query_contamination: **TRAP: means different things by tier.** Tier 3: abbreviation-collision rows (40, wrong 'ASD'). Tier 4: screening-uncertain rows (1,960). Two different concepts under one name.
column_descriptions.screen_verdict_uncertain: Tier 4: the screen was uncertain whether the paper is in scope.

notes: Identifiers were requested FROM THE MODEL. This is the defect that Tiers 3-4 fixed.
Accept-header bug present: some papers silently downgraded to abstract-only.
Identifiers requested from the model; 27.7% of ontology ids and ~34% of HPO ids were fabricated, then repaired syntactically.
Accept-header bug cost 57 papers, later recovered by re-extraction (314 -> 693 findings).
Same pipeline and prompt as Part A. 64 chunks, 46,579s wall, 64/64 completed, zero permanent failures.
**The model emits NAMES ONLY.** Every identifier is derived afterwards by authority lookup. A parser guard rejects any id-shaped string the model returns anyway.
Accept header fixed to `*/*`, with a non-empty >2000-char assertion before treating a paper as abstract-only.
`blocked` made retryable, with the HTTP status recorded in `fetch_note`.
Full text discarded after extraction — the one fix not made.
**Body text RETAINED** in gzipped chunk archives. This is why Tier 4 is the only package with 100% quote verifiability.
Papers pre-screened by a rule+LLM instrument before extraction, because Tier 4's themes sit at the corpus boundary.

Screening instrument was itself repaired mid-run: a closed in-scope condition list read as exhaustive and the model excluded familial dysautonomia from a dysautonomia corpus (303 off-topic vs the rule arm's 20). The 303-vs-20 disagreement was the tell that the instrument was broken, not the papers.

methods_validation_checks: 2. **Conservation** — no chunk silently absent, no chunk exceeding its paper allotment.
3. **Monotonicity** — a pass that adds must never shrink counts.
4. **No model-emitted identifiers** — no id-shaped string in any name field.
5. **Identifier provenance** — every non-null identifier carries a source tag.
7. **Duplicates** — on the FULL row. A loose key flags legitimate distinct findings drawn from
one summary sentence, which was a false defect reading in Tier 2.
8. **HPO multi-value consistency** — `hpo_id_count` equals the delimiter count.
9. **Authority/prefix agreement** — an identifier's prefix must match the authority its
provenance names. Added after an audit found 49 rows claiming `authority_lookup_ols_hp`
while holding GO/PATO/MPATH ids: the ids were right, the provenance CLAIM was wrong, and
the eight-check suite could not see it because it only verified that a source tag exists,
never that it agrees with the identifier it labels.
limitations_enum_drift_tail: verbatim, never coerced.** Two of the drifted values are arguments that the enum is
deficient rather than the output wrong — `other patient group` (findings about another
disease used as a mechanistic analogy, which the enum has no slot for) and `IBD_gut`
(probably an `IBS_gut` typo, but IBD and IBS are different diseases so correcting it would
change what the row claims). Both are formally unadjudicated.
limitations_cross_package_traps: Three columns will mislead you if you pool packages naively. Full detail in
- **`id_resolved_frac` ranks the packages backwards.** It measures coverage, not correctness.
- **`ontology_id_source == 'unresolved_nulled'`** means identifier KEPT in Tier 2 and
identifier NULLED in Tiers 3-4. The obvious filter drops 2,242 Tier-2 rows that do carry
- **`query_contamination`** means abbreviation collision in Tier 3 (40 rows) and screening
uncertainty in Tier 4 (1,960 rows). Two concepts, one name.
Eleven metrics are not comparable across all five packages. Five aggregates are safe.
limitations_corpus_construction: The corpus was assembled by keyword query, so it inherits every bias of the queries: it is
**English-language, PubMed/Europe-PMC-indexed, and weighted toward the conditions that were
searched for**. Conditions appear in packages other than their own only as incidental
mentions — a count of `condition == 'fibromyalgia'` in the Tier 1 package means
*POTS/dysautonomia papers that mention fibromyalgia*, not the fibromyalgia literature.
Publication bias is inherited wholesale and unmeasured. Null results are retained where the
source reported them (`null_or_failed_result`), which partially offsets this — but only
partially, since unpublished nulls are absent by construction.

tier1: **This package is already deployed** — it is the site's tier-1 layer, rows 0–36,458.
**But the row counts differ: this package has 36,067 rows, the site's tier-1 layer has
{t1_rows}.** A {t1_delta}-row delta. The site was built from the pre-harmonization
tier-1 export (89 columns); this package is the harmonized slice (107 columns). Do **not**
assume row *i* here is row *i* on the site. If you rebuild the site from this package, you
rebuild the whole row-order contract and every embedding shard with it.
**Nothing new to load.** What this package offers the site is *corrections*, not content:
| identifier honesty | id present or absent | `ontology_id_verification` distinguishes model-emitted from authority-verified |
| quote verifiability | not surfaced | `cap_quote_source_retained` per row |
### The one change worth making for tier 1
The site presents tier-1 ontology identifiers with no signal that **~42% of them do not
denote their entity**. That is the most misleading thing on the site today. A reader
clicking an entity gets an identifier that looks authoritative.
Minimum fix, Layer 3 only, no rebuild: badge tier-1 identifiers as unverified wherever they
render. `ui.js` already exports `framingBanner()` and `entityCoverageNote()`; add a third
tier2a: **This package is already deployed** — it is the site's tier-2 layer, rows
**{t2a_rows}**, which is this package's row count to the row.
**This resolves an ambiguity in the site's own copy.** The deployed scope caveat reads
*"Tier-2 covers 81 of 146 chunks (~55%)"*. That is precisely this package: Part A, 81
chunks. The missing ~45% is **Tier 2 Part B**, which exists, is complete, and is simply not
**Nothing new to load from this package.** Its value to the site is that the caveat can now
name what is missing instead of gesturing at a percentage.
Replace the `~55%` framing in `framingBanner()` with something a reader can act on:
> Tier 2 was extracted in two waves. This site currently shows the first wave — 81 of 145
> chunks, {t2a_rows} findings from 3,123 papers. The second wave (64 chunks, 33,830 findings,
> 2,589 papers) is complete and published separately, but is not loaded here. The two waves
> share no papers and cover the same nine themes.
tier2b: **This package is NOT on the site. It is the single largest content addition available.**
The site's *"Tier-2 covers 81 of 146 chunks (~55%)"* caveat exists because of this
package. Loading it retires that caveat.
| | current site | after adding this package |
| findings | {cur_findings} | **{after_findings}** |
| papers | {cur_papers} | **{after_papers}** |
| tier-2 coverage | 81 of 145 chunks | **145 of 145** |
| shards @ {shard_rows} rows | {cur_shards} | **{after_shards}** |
Because the two waves share **zero papers**, this is a pure append — no dedup pass, no
paper-record merge.
### Load procedure
The row-order contract is **append-only**, so Part B goes after row 73,069 and every
existing row index stays valid:
rows      0 – 36,458   tier 1        (unchanged)
rows {t1_rows} – 73,069   tier 2 part A (unchanged)
rows {cur_findings} – 106,899  tier 2 part B (new)
1. Append this package's rows to the Layer 1 record in that order.
2. Regenerate Layer 2 wholesale — `site/data/*.json`, all shards, `emb/*.bin`. Bump
`meta.json` version from `{cur_version}` to `combined-t1t2ab-1`.
3. Re-embed. Existing embedding shards stay byte-valid (append-only), so only the new
shards need computing.
4. Run `site_tools/` verification before publishing.
5. Update `framingBanner()` — the ~55% caveat is now false and must not survive the load.
**Watch the facet keys.** `ti` (tier) and `sl` (source_literature) exist but are documented
as not load-bearing. Both waves are `ti = t2`, so a tier facet will not distinguish them.
If you want the waves separable in the UI, that is a **new facet**, not a reuse of `ti`.
tier3: **This package is NOT on the site.** It is the first content from the post-tier-2
pipeline, and it changes what the site can honestly claim about identifiers.
| | current site | after adding this package |
| findings | {cur_findings} | **{after_findings}** |
| papers | {cur_papers} | **{after_papers}** |
| shards @ {shard_rows} rows | {cur_shards} | **{after_shards}** |
### What is genuinely new for the site
1. **Authority-verified identifiers — 4,113 rows.** Everything on the site today is
model-emitted. These are resolver-derived and score 0.986 on denotation. This is the
first time the site could show a *verified* badge that means something.
2. **`canonical_entity` populated in-row — 17,828 rows.** The site's 2,803 canonical
entities were computed at build time from a vocabulary join. Tier 3 carries
canonicalization in the data itself.
3. **`entity_kind`** — gene / protein / chemical / anatomical. A facet the site cannot
currently offer at all. Absent (null, not false) for tiers 1–2.
4. **`certainty_derived`** — hedge detection over finding text *and* quote. Enables a
confidence filter that does not exist today.
5. **Long COVID becomes the site's largest condition** — this package is long-COVID
dominated, and pooling shifts the corpus's centre of gravity.
### Two traps specific to loading tier 3
**Trap A — `entity_kind` and `certainty_derived` are null for every row already on the
site.** A facet built on either will silently show only tier-3 rows. Gate on the `cap_*`
flags, and label the facet as tier-3-onward, or a reader will read *"12 genes"* as a
corpus-wide count when it is a tier-3 count.
**Trap B — mixing verified and unverified identifiers in one entity view.** Once tier 3 is
loaded the site holds both kinds. An entity page pooling them presents 0.986-grade and
0.578-grade identifiers identically. **Split them in the UI, or badge every one.**
**Also filter `query_contamination`** — 40 rows from 6 papers pulled in by the ambiguous
abbreviation *ASD* (adult spinal deformity / atrial septal defect, not autism). They should
not surface in an autism view. `scope/tier3_offtopic_pmids.csv` lists the 28 PMIDs.
tier4: **This package is NOT on the site.** It is small, but it is the only package whose quotes
are all verifiable — which is a *feature the site cannot currently offer for any row*.

### What is genuinely new for the site
1. **100% quote verifiability — 15,646 rows.** Body text was retained, so every quote can
be re-checked against its own source. Every other row on the site has a quote whose
source is gone. This supports a *"verified against source"* badge that is true.
2. **The highest identifier correctness in the corpus** — 0.998, though at the lowest
coverage (10.3%).
3. **Four themes absent from the site**: migraine intersection, hypermobility spectrum,
Sjögren's, PANS/PANDAS.
4. **`screen_verdict_uncertain`** — 1,960 rows the screening instrument was unsure about.
Surfacing this honestly is better than hiding it.
### Traps specific to loading tier 4
**`query_contamination` means something different here.** In tier 3 it marks abbreviation
collisions (40 rows); in tier 4 it marks screening uncertainty (1,960 rows). **A single
site-wide filter on this column would conflate two unrelated concepts.** Read
`screen_verdict_uncertain` for tier 4 instead.
**Coverage has two true values** — 85.97% of screened papers, 74.57% of the pre-screening
universe. If the site states a tier-4 coverage figure it must say which.
